To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the model developed for the LICCHUS engine is adequate for predicting the dynamic behavior of the compressor and the surge phenomena, and that the model is adequate for the development and design of active surge controllers.
the model developed herein is adequate for the purposes of design, simulation, and analysis of active surge control and rotating stall avoidance systems for single spool, turbojet engines.
the model we have developed can be used to simulate surge phenomena, and that this model can be used to design and evaluate active surge control systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the design of active control systems for the prevention of compressor stall and surge in turbojet engines.
the development of a model which will be used to design active surge control systems for aircraft gas turbine engines.
the development of an analytical model which will provide the basis for the design of active control systems for surge and rotating stall avoidance in aircraft engines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this model is adequate for design of active surge avoidance systems, and that it is not adequate for the design and analysis of rotating stall avoidance.
the model is adequate for the purpose of designing active surge control/ rotating stall avoidance systems in single spool centrifugal compressor turbojet engines.

the model developed herein is capable of predicting the response of the engine to the control inputs and is adequate for the purpose of designing active surge control and/or rotating stall avoidance systems in gas turbine engines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model developed herein is adequate for use in the preliminary design of active surge and rotating stall avoidance systems in gas turbine engines.
the model has been shown to be adequate for the design and analysis of active surge control systems.
we have developed a quasi one dimensional model of an aircraft gas turbine engine with sufficient fidelity to be useful in the design of surge control/rotatng stall avoidance systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model can be used as a tool in the design and evaluation of active surge control and rotating stall avoidance systems for aircraft gas turbine engines.
the model is useful in the design of control systems for active surge control/avoidance and rotating stall avoidance.
the model is adequate to serve as the basis for a controller design.
